purpose: Guided positive Catholic doctrine in a coherent order between the Daily Catechism and the full Traditional Catechism reference.

publication_gate.rule: Do not expose learn.faith until every lesson has resolved Catechism references, paragraph-level sources, bilingual publication-ready text and cross-module deduplication.
publication_gate.note: All 54 lessons now have bilingual source-linked draft prose and exact St Pius X mappings. Publication remains blocked pending final editorial review, source-link verification and deduplication acceptance.

relationship_to_existing.learn.catechism.daily: Daily review and spaced encounter with the existing question bank; not the guided doctrine course.
relationship_to_existing.learn.catechism: Full searchable Traditional Catechism reference and exact Q&A owner.
relationship_to_existing.learn.faith: Guided synthesis only; it references rather than replaces or duplicates the Catechism corpus.
relationship_to_existing.apologetics: Defence against objections; not positive doctrinal instruction.
relationship_to_existing.church-crisis: Contested development, rupture/continuity and authority questions; not baseline doctrine.

source_policy.primary_doctrine: Use the existing Traditional Catechism corpus as the immediate doctrinal reference layer, then resolve substantive prose to original Scripture, councils, catechisms and authoritative Magisterium where available.
source_policy.paragraph_rule: Every substantive published paragraph must carry explicit source support.

lessons.catechismNote: St Pius X gives the attributes and providence of God, not a developed philosophical proof of God's existence.

lessons.supplementarySourceNeed: The 1912 catechism presupposes Revelation more than it systematically defines revelation, inspiration and transmission; supplement with authoritative doctrinal sources.

PIUS_X_1912.title: St Pius X — Catechism of Christian Doctrine (1912), 433-question shorter catechism

VATICAN_I_DEI_FILIUS_CH2.title: First Vatican Council — Dei Filius, ch. II (Revelation)
VATICAN_I_DEI_FILIUS_CH2.note: Supports the Church's teaching that God can be known with certainty from created things by the natural light of human reason, while supernatural Revelation remains distinct and necessary for man's supernatural end.

LEO_XIII_LIBERTAS.title: Leo XIII — Libertas praestantissimum (1888)
LEO_XIII_LIBERTAS.note: Used for freedom, law and the natural law as rational participation in the eternal law.

VERITATIS_SPLENDOR_60_61.title: John Paul II — Veritatis splendor §§60–61
VERITATIS_SPLENDOR_60_61.note: Used for the judgment of conscience as witness to objective moral truth rather than creator of moral law.

CCC_1868_COOPERATION.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church §1868 — Cooperation in the sins of others
CCC_1868_COOPERATION.note: Used narrowly to distinguish responsibility for another person's sin through direct participation, counsel/approval, culpable omission, or protection of wrongdoing.

PIUS_XII_MUNIFICENTISSIMUS_DEUS.title: Pius XII — Munificentissimus Deus (1950)
PIUS_XII_MUNIFICENTISSIMUS_DEUS.note: Used for the defined dogma of the bodily Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary, especially §44.

PIUS_XII_MEDIATOR_DEI_165.title: Pius XII — Mediator Dei §165
PIUS_XII_MEDIATOR_DEI_165.note: Used for the theological meaning of the liturgical year as Christ's mysteries living in the Church, not merely a record of past events.
